Check rating data before fitting an MFRM

Source: R/api-estimation.R
describe_mfrm_data.Rd

Audit row retention, missingness, score category support, duplicate Person-by-facet cells, Person-facet graph connectivity, optional observed agreement, and optional prospective interaction contrast identifiability before calling fit_mfrm().

Usage

describe_mfrm_data(
  data,
  person = NULL,
  facets = NULL,
  score = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  rating_min = NULL,
  rating_max = NULL,
  keep_original = FALSE,
  missing_codes = NULL,
  include_person_facet = FALSE,
  include_agreement = TRUE,
  rater_facet = NULL,
  context_facets = NULL,
  agreement_top_n = NULL,
  expected_design = NULL,
  min_linking_persons = 2L,
  category_policy = NULL,
  repeated_ratings = c("review", "independent"),
  comparisons = NULL,
  spec = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_data_description'
summary(object, digits = 3, top_n = 10, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_data_description'
plot(
  x,
  y = NULL,
  type = c("score_distribution", "facet_levels", "missing"),
  main = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  label_angle = 45,
  draw = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Long-format rating data.frame (one row per rating event).

person

Data column names, rubric bounds, category handling ("collapse" vs "preserve"), duplicate-cell policy ("review" vs "independent"), and sentinel recoding; shared with fit_mfrm() via spec (see fit_mfrm_technical_details).

facets

Data column names, rubric bounds, category handling ("collapse" vs "preserve"), duplicate-cell policy ("review" vs "independent"), and sentinel recoding; shared with fit_mfrm() via spec (see fit_mfrm_technical_details).

score

Data column names, rubric bounds, category handling ("collapse" vs "preserve"), duplicate-cell policy ("review" vs "independent"), and sentinel recoding; shared with fit_mfrm() via spec (see fit_mfrm_technical_details).

Data column names, rubric bounds, category handling ("collapse" vs "preserve"), duplicate-cell policy ("review" vs "independent"), and sentinel recoding; shared with fit_mfrm() via spec (see fit_mfrm_technical_details).

rating_min

Data column names, rubric bounds, category handling ("collapse" vs "preserve"), duplicate-cell policy ("review" vs "independent"), and sentinel recoding; shared with fit_mfrm() via spec (see fit_mfrm_technical_details).

rating_max

Data column names, rubric bounds, category handling ("collapse" vs "preserve"), duplicate-cell policy ("review" vs "independent"), and sentinel recoding; shared with fit_mfrm() via spec (see fit_mfrm_technical_details).

keep_original

Data column names, rubric bounds, category handling ("collapse" vs "preserve"), duplicate-cell policy ("review" vs "independent"), and sentinel recoding; shared with fit_mfrm() via spec (see fit_mfrm_technical_details).

Data column names, rubric bounds, category handling ("collapse" vs "preserve"), duplicate-cell policy ("review" vs "independent"), and sentinel recoding; shared with fit_mfrm() via spec (see fit_mfrm_technical_details).

Controls for including Person rows in facet_level_summary and computing observed scorer agreement across matched context_facets.

Controls for including Person rows in facet_level_summary and computing observed scorer agreement across matched context_facets.

Controls for including Person rows in facet_level_summary and computing observed scorer agreement across matched context_facets.

Controls for including Person rows in facet_level_summary and computing observed scorer agreement across matched context_facets.

Controls for including Person rows in facet_level_summary and computing observed scorer agreement across matched context_facets.

Optional planned assignment roster data.frame (for structural_missingness) and sparse-link Person count flag (linkage_summary$SparseLevels).

min_linking_persons

Optional planned assignment roster data.frame (for structural_missingness) and sparse-link Person count flag (linkage_summary$SparseLevels).

category_policy

Data column names, rubric bounds, category handling ("collapse" vs "preserve"), duplicate-cell policy ("review" vs "independent"), and sentinel recoding; shared with fit_mfrm() via spec (see fit_mfrm_technical_details).

Data column names, rubric bounds, category handling ("collapse" vs "preserve"), duplicate-cell policy ("review" vs "independent"), and sentinel recoding; shared with fit_mfrm() via spec (see fit_mfrm_technical_details).

comparisons

Optional list(facet = ..., group = ..., groups = c("A", "B"), contrasts = W, model = ..., method = ...) reviewing prospective facet-by-origin interaction contrasts (IdentificationBasis: free_person_response_model, population_restriction, conditional_support, unidentified, not_evaluated, unsupported) for fit_mfrm(fit_scope = "comparisons", comparison_review = ...).

spec

Optional shared model-specification list accepted by fit_mfrm(), review_mfrm_anchors(), and export_mfrm_model().

Number of digits for numeric rounding.

Maximum rows shown in preview blocks.

y

Reserved for generic compatibility.

Plot type: "score_distribution", "facet_levels", or "missing".

Optional named colors (score, facet, missing).

label_angle

X-axis label angle for bar plots.

If TRUE, display the returned ggplot.

Value

An mfrm_data_description list (summary(), plot()) with overview (CategoryPolicy, ScoreRecoded), missing_by_column, missing_rate_summary, score_descriptives, weight_descriptives, score_distribution, facet_level_summary, facet_crosstabs, linkage_summary, structural_missingness, design_connectivity, design_components, duplicate_cell_summary, duplicate_cell_detail, agreement, row_retention, preparation_notes, missing_recoding, score_support, and optional comparison_review.

For summary(): An object of class summary.mfrm_data_description.

  • overview: design/sample counts

  • missing: top columns by missingness

  • score_distribution: compact score-usage table, including zero-count categories retained by the prepared score support

  • facet_overview: facet-level coverage summary

  • structural_missingness: declared assignment coverage summary; status is "not_declared" when no assignment roster was supplied

  • structural_level_coverage: expected versus observed level counts

  • design_connectivity: Person-facet component counts for observed and declared-expected designs

  • design_components: component sizes and facet-level labels; person labels are suppressed unless explicitly requested in describe_mfrm_data()

  • linkage_summary: sparse-support and shared-person counts by facet

  • duplicate_cell_summary: aggregate duplicate-cell counts

  • agreement: selected-facet agreement summary when available

  • agreement_settings: selected scorer facet, matching context, and status

  • row_retention: row counts before and after preparation filters

  • preparation_notes: structured preparation notes retained from describe_mfrm_data()

  • reporting_map: manuscript-oriented guide to what is covered here versus which companion outputs should be consulted

  • caveats: structured warning/review rows for score-support issues; print(summary(ds)) shows a compact Caveats block when rows are present

  • notes: plain-language explanations of missingness, preparation, score support, and design-review findings

For plot(): A ggplot object (invisibly), with underlying plot tables accessible via plot_data().

Details

summary() provides compact previews; the reading order and field differences are described under "Reading the data review".

plot() method: Plot a data-description object

Reading data-review plots

  • "score_distribution" plots WeightedN, the sum of weights per category. Sparse categories limit threshold information, but uniformity/unimodality is not required. Read floor/ceiling concentrations against rubric, assignments and target population; this is not a sample-adequacy test.

  • "facet_levels" shows distinct levels per facet. Check expected levels, ratings per level and crossings: more levels increase parameter dimension, while more optimizer iterations cannot repair missing identification.

  • "missing" plots input missing counts. Investigate them using the tables above; missing scores/Persons/facet IDs cause row exclusions in fitting.

See also

fit_mfrm(), fit_mfrm_technical_details, recode_missing_codes(), review_mfrm_anchors()

describe_mfrm_data(), summary.mfrm_fit()

describe_mfrm_data(), plot_data()

Examples

library(mfrmr)
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")
head(ratings)
#>                Study Person Rater    Criterion Score Group
#> 1 OperationalExample   P001   R01     Language     4     A
#> 2 OperationalExample   P001   R01 Organization     2     A
#> 3 OperationalExample   P001   R02      Content     4     A
#> 4 OperationalExample   P001   R02     Language     3     A
#> 5 OperationalExample   P001   R02 Organization     2     A
#> 6 OperationalExample   P002   R01      Content     3     A

# Check the data before fitting; the intended score categories are 1 to 4
data_review <- describe_mfrm_data(
  data = ratings,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score",
  rating_min = 1,
  rating_max = 4,
  category_policy = "preserve"
)
data_review$row_retention       # Input and retained rows; check DroppedRows
#>                             Stage Rows DroppedRows
#> 1          input_selected_columns  282           0
#> 2 after_missing_and_weight_filter  282           0
#>                            DroppedReason
#> 1                                       
#> 2 missing values or non-positive weights
data_review$missing_by_column   # Missing input values in each model column
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#>   Column    Missing
#>   <chr>       <int>
#> 1 Person          0
#> 2 Rater           0
#> 3 Criterion       0
#> 4 Score           0
data_review$score_distribution  # RawN is the number of ratings per category
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   Score  RawN WeightedN Percent
#>   <int> <int>     <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1     1    62        62    22.0
#> 2     2    96        96    34.0
#> 3     3    78        78    27.7
#> 4     4    46        46    16.3
data_review$design_connectivity # Components = 1 means connected for that facet
#>      Basis     Facet PersonNodes FacetLevelNodes Edges Components
#> 1 observed     Rater          48               6    96          1
#> 2 observed Criterion          48               3   144          1
#>   LargestComponentPersons LargestComponentLevels LargestComponentPercent
#> 1                      48                      6                     100
#> 2                      48                      3                     100
#>   Connected
#> 1      TRUE
#> 2      TRUE
# Here all 282 rows are retained, and all four categories have observations

# Save a compact summary when you want the overview and review notes
review <- summary(data_review)
review$overview
#>   Observations TotalWeight Persons Facets Categories RatingMin RatingMax
#> 1          282         282      48      2          4         1         4
#>   RatingRangeSource RatingMinSource RatingMaxSource CategoryPolicy ScoreRecoded
#> 1          declared        declared        declared       preserve        FALSE
review$notes
#> [1] "No missing values were detected in selected input columns."                                                                                                  
#> [2] "Structural missingness was not assessed because `expected_design` was not supplied. Absent rows cannot be distinguished from cells that were never assigned."
# For the next fit, use data = ratings; data_review is a set of checks, not ratings
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("summary.mfrm_data_description", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(mfrmr)
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")

# Demonstrate two missing scores in a copy of the example data
ratings$Score[1:2] <- NA
data_review <- describe_mfrm_data(
  data = ratings,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score",
  rating_min = 1,
  rating_max = 4,
  category_policy = "preserve"
)
review <- summary(data_review)
review$row_retention # 282 input rows, 280 retained rows
review$missing       # Score has 2 missing input values
review$overview      # Counts describe the retained ratings
review$notes         # Explanations to read before fitting

# The original description retains the full missingness table
data_review$missing_by_column
# Investigate missingness before using ratings in fit_mfrm()
} # }
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("plot.mfrm_data_description", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
ds <- describe_mfrm_data(toy, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score")
p <- plot(ds, draw = FALSE)
} # }
